text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- National Assembly adopted the Vietnam's first value added tax law, which will come into effect on January 1, 1999.
-- Vietnam's industrial sector has attracted $12 billion in direct foreign investment, accounting for 44 percent of the country's total direct foreign investment.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet issued an order on April 26 on preparations for, and organisation of, July elections to the National Assembly.
-- The Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs issued a new circular on shortening working hours for people involved in intensive or hazardous labour from eight to six hours a day.
-- Vietnam's Politburo issued a notice on the continuous, active and firm deployment of the equitisation of state-owned enterprises.

-- Vice prime Minister Nguyen Khanh said to the Assistant of United Nation High Comissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) that he hoped UNHCR would continue supporting humanitarian activities through medium- and small-scale projects in Vietnam.
-- According to a new circular issued by Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs, Vietnamese people working abroad on a fixed-term contract, should pay social insurance from their wages.
